newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM bids to put Italian air cargo on rail.
newsitem.headline: KLM bids to put Italian air cargo on rail.

text.p: KLM Cargo has entered into an agreement to send airfreight by rail between Italy and the Netherlands.
The cooperative agreement has been formed with leading European air freight truckert Jan De Rijk and privately owned Dutch rail company, Trailstar.
"The trial starts in June and this is a first for KLM Cargo. It is very exciting for us," said a KLM spokesman.
Twenty special wagons are being built and KLM expects that around 12 containers a week will travel from Milan to Rotterdam
When the airfreight arrives in Rotterdam, KLM Cargo will then truck it to Schiphol Airport.
Operational coordination of the project is being carried out by Jan De Rijk. The Dutch trucking company handles KLM Cargo's airfreight throughout Europe.
The rail transport is being carried out by Trailstar which operates daily shuttles between Italy and the Netherlands.
It is expected that the shuttles will travel on the weekends when many European countries now have trucking bans in place and because of severe weekend road traffic congestion.
The journey time between Italy and the Netherlands is expected to take 24 hours.

KLM Cargo's spokesman stressed that this is an experiment. "We will have to see how practical it is to move airfreight over the rails. But the congestion on the roads means this could be very valuable."
If the experiment is a success other destinations in Europe will be considered.
Fashion and hi-tech goods are expected to major exports travelling via the new system.
